leo_cs: Customer kickoff in 8h. Need a one-page "Ops Ready" cheat we can drop in their runbook: prefill, safe batching defaults, KV cache guidance, streaming tips, 72h watchlist, and 3-step mitigations. Make it ops-friendly.

anya_se: I can draft. Keep bullets, copy-paste snippets, and tiny validation checks. No internal flags; only hosted + dedicated knobs.

mike_sre: Add a simple degraded flow that ops can run without eng: route failover, throttle, compact fallback. Also include check for prefix_cache_hit_rate.

vika_support: I'll paste top 5 customer questions we've seen this quarter (one-line answers).

anya_se: Draft (compact):

"Ops Ready 0000Cheat Sheet"
- Goal: stabilize cost & latency in first 72h. Catch regressions early.
- Prefill (copy/paste): run a short prefill to warm ~10-15% active users and capture baseline tokens/day:
  for i in $(seq 1 120); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"welcome","max_tokens":64,"metadata":{"prefill":true}}' & done; wait
- Batching defaults (hosted + dedicated):
  * short prompts (<80 tokens): target_batch_size=20, max_batch_wait_ms=25
  * long outputs (>512 tokens): target_batch_size=4, max_batch_wait_ms=10
- KV cache: enable prefix_cache=true; prefix_ttl_seconds=300 for interactive flows, 45s for high-churn. Aim for prefix_cache_hit_rate >40% after prefill.
- Streaming: enable for human-facing long outputs (>512 tokens); set keepalive_seconds=12 and socket_timeout_ms=45000. Confirm proxies allow long connections.
- Cost controls: set daily_token_limit and per_minute_cap; add alert at 60% of daily usage.
- 72h watchlist (if any 2 of these occur, treat as elevated risk):
  1) tokens/day > baseline * 1.35 for 24h
  2) P95 latency > SLO for 2+ hours
  3) sustained 5xx rate > 1% for 30+ minutes
- Fast mitigations (do in order):
  1) Switch routing to alternate region with capacity (Console routing -> failover).
  2) Enable throttles: per-client_rate_limit=100 req/min and temporary daily_token_limit reduction.
  3) Enable compact fallback model and reduce max_generation_tokens by ~25%.
- What to include when contacting support: sample request JSON, route.name, account_id, X-Request-ID, prompt_hash, and approximate timestamps.

mike_sre: Minimal validation commands ops can run: 
- Check KV hit rate: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/metrics?name=prefix_cache_hit_rate
- Compare warm vs cold latency: run 30 warm requests vs 30 cold and compare median latencies.
- Test alerting: simulate token burn to 61% and confirm webhook to ops endpoint.

vika_support: Top-5 FAQs (one-line answers):
1) Tokens jumped after integration? -> Often duplicated prompts or verbose system text; enable client dedupe and prefill.
2) Warm pools ineffective? -> Verify prefix_cache_hit_rate and confirm prefill volume.
3) Streaming stalls? -> Increase keepalive_seconds and check LB/proxy buffering.
4) How to limit spend during pilot? -> Configure daily_token_limit + per_minute_cap and alerts.
5) High latency variance? -> Review batch sizes and cache hit metrics; consider lowering max_batch_tokens.

paul_pm: Add escalation: if two watchlist signals occur within 72h, open ticket tagged cs:ops-review. CS+Eng will run a config audit and can apply short-term protections.

anya_se: Small copy-paste config snippet for Console integrations (JSON blob): { "runtime": ["batching: target_batch_size=20,max_batch_wait_ms=25" , "kv_cache: prefix_cache=true,prefix_ttl_seconds=300" , "streaming: enabled=true,keepalive_s=12"] }
